title: BJP Leads in Over 100 Kolkata Civic Wards
excerpt: Riding a historic state election sweep, BJP now leads in more than 100 of Kolkata's 144 municipal wards — a seismic reversal from 2021.
body:
Kolkata's political map shifted dramatically this month. Buoyed by the BJP's landslide in the West Bengal Assembly Election, analysis of ward-level results shows the party now leading across roughly 101-102 of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation's 144 wards — compared to just three seats it held after the 2021 civic polls.

**What the numbers show:**
Bengali daily Anandabazar Patrika's ward-level analysis, cited by The Federal, found the BJP leading in 101 of 144 KMC wards, with the TMC reduced to just 43. The assembly election itself told the same story: in the Presidency belt, which includes the city of Kolkata, the BJP led in 52 out of 108 seats — a stark contrast to the eight seats it won in 2021. In the 2021 KMC elections, the TMC had pocketed 134 of the 144 wards, while the BJP got only three.

**Why Kolkata matters:**
Following the two-phase polling on April 23 and April 29, the BJP secured a historic landslide in the West Bengal Assembly Elections, ending 15 years of TMC rule, sweeping 206 seats and comfortably crossing the majority mark of 147. TMC sources acknowledge it may struggle to hold the KMC, barring areas such as Kasba, Tiljala, Khidirpore and others with a sizeable minority population. This marks the first time the BJP has been elected in the state since assembly elections first began in 1937.

**What to watch:**
The 2026 Kolkata Municipal Corporation election is tentatively scheduled for December 2026, and with the new BJP state government now in place under Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, a full saffron takeover of India's third-largest city government looks increasingly likely.
